rules.cwe_name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
rules.description: Detects Weak key generation key size (< 2048 bits)

rules.cwe_name: Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers
rules.description: Tokens used for sensitive tasks, such as, password recovery, and email confirmation, should not use predictable values.

rules.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
rules.description: Finds uses of symmetric cryptography algorithms that are weak, obsolete, or otherwise unaccepted. The key lengths allowed are 128, 192, and 256 bits. These are all the key lengths supported by AES, so any application of AES is considered acceptable.

rules.cwe_name: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
rules.description: Using a cryptographically weak pseudo-random number generator to generate a security-sensitive value may allow an attacker to predict what value will be generated.

rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
rules.description: A string formatting operation, such as '"%s: %s, %s" % (a,b)', where the number of conversion specifiers in the format string differs from the number of values to be formatted will raise a TypeError.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Certificate Validation
rules.description: Accepting unknown host keys can allow man-in-the-middle attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Cryptographic Issues
rules.description: Legacy category for cryptographic design or implementation weaknesses.

rules.cwe_name: Dead Code
rules.description: A statement has no effect

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Using jinja2 templates with 'autoescape=False' can cause a cross-site scripting vulnerability.
